header.label: Company Name
header.prompt: What's the name of the company or business?
header.hint: If there's a parent company or operating entity, get the exact legal name.

header.label: Concept
header.prompt: What concept or brand are we talking about?

header.label: Seller Contact Name
header.prompt: Who are we speaking with — the seller's name?
header.hint: Get their full name and confirm how they spell it. Identify their role (owner, operator, broker).

header.label: RRG Rep
header.prompt: Which RRG rep is running this call?

header.label: Metro
header.prompt: Which market or metro is this in?

questions.label: Concept Type
questions.prompt: What type of concept is it — quick service, full service, bar?
questions.hint: Listen for service style, average check size, and operating model. This impacts buyer profile and valuation.

questions.label: Franchise or Independent?
questions.prompt: Is it a franchise or independent?
questions.hint: Franchises have brand restrictions and franchisor approval needed for sale. Independents have more buyer flexibility but less brand equity.

questions.label: Owner’s Role
questions.prompt: How involved is the owner day to day?
questions.hint: Clarify if owner works on-site, from a distance, or not at all. This affects buyer profile and transition risk.

questions.label: Ownership Structure
questions.prompt: How is ownership structured — sole owner, partners?
questions.hint: Partnerships and family businesses need full buy-in on sale terms. Multiple owners = longer deal timeline. Get names of all decision-makers.

questions.label: Real Estate
questions.prompt: Do they own the real estate, or lease the space?
questions.hint: Owners have added value to sell. Lessees depend on lease terms—critical for deal. "Owns + Leases" is complex; clarify which locations are owned vs leased.

questions.label: Years in Operation
questions.prompt: How many years have they been in operation?
questions.hint: Newer businesses (< 3 years) are riskier to buyers. Established businesses (5+ years) have proven track records. Ask about ownership tenure specifically.

questions.label: Number of Locations
questions.prompt: How many locations do they operate?
questions.hint: Multi-unit operators have higher valuation. Single location = simpler sale. Get names and status (owned, leased, closed) of all locations.

questions.label: Approx. Employees
questions.prompt: Roughly how many employees do they have?
questions.hint: Employee count indicates business scale and labor intensity. High turnover or key staff dependencies are red flags. Ask about management depth.

questions.label: Primary Motivation for Selling
questions.prompt: What's their main reason for selling?
questions.hint: Motivation reveals deal urgency and risk. Financial distress or disputes can indicate hidden problems. Retirement signals transition prep time.

questions.label: Motivation (Rep’s Own Words)
questions.prompt: In your own words — what’s really driving this sale?
questions.hint: Listen for what’s NOT being said. Burnout signals lifestyle buyer appeal. Burnout + aggressive timeline = distressed deal risk. Write what you actually hear.

questions.label: Timeline
questions.prompt: What's their timeline to sell?
questions.hint: Urgent timelines can mean distressed deals or serious intent. Long timelines allow for preparation and financial cleanup.

questions.label: Exit Type
questions.prompt: What kind of exit are they after — full sale, partial, walk away?
questions.hint: Full exit is cleanest. Earn-outs and stay-on arrangements = transition risk and buyer friction. Real estate-only flips the buyer profile entirely.

questions.label: Profitability
questions.prompt: Is the business profitable right now?
questions.hint: Ask about net profit after all expenses. If not profitable, probe for reasons (temporary, systemic issues, or accounting choices).

questions.label: Financial Records Available?
questions.prompt: Do they have clean financial records available?
questions.hint: This is critical for buyers and valuation. 'Disorganized' is a major red flag—will need reconstruction work before any buyer can move forward.

questions.label: Annual Revenue
questions.prompt: Roughly what are their annual sales?
questions.hint: Ask for top-line sales and clarify if this includes alcohol, takeout, catering. Get a range if exact figures aren't available.

questions.label: Sales vs. Prior Year
questions.prompt: How are sales trending versus last year?
questions.hint: Down sales can justify the sale or signal structural problems. Up sales make it harder to justify exit—dig deeper on motivation if trending up.

questions.label: Earnings Basis
questions.prompt: What earnings basis are we using — SDE, EBITDA, cash flow?
questions.hint: Owner’s Take is highest for seller but not buyer-friendly. EBITDA/SDE require documentation. Clarify what owner is actually pulling out per month.

questions.label: Earnings Figure (Approx.)
questions.prompt: Roughly what are the annual earnings on that basis?
questions.hint: Get a specific number or range. Earnings drive valuation—accuracy here matters. Ask if figure includes/excludes owner salary, benefits, or personal expenses.

questions.label: Earnings vs. Prior Year
questions.prompt: How are earnings trending versus last year?
questions.hint: Downward earnings + immediate sale = red flag for structural issues. Flat/up earnings with experienced buyer = smoother transition.

questions.label: Debt, Liens, Lawsuits, or Unusual Items?
questions.prompt: Any debt, liens, lawsuits, or anything unusual?
questions.hint: Debt must clear at close—impacts net proceeds. Liens and lawsuits kill deals. Don't let "Unsure" slide; they know their own balance sheet. Press for specifics.

questions.label: Debt / Lien / Lawsuit Details
questions.prompt: Tell me more about that debt or legal item.
questions.hint: Get amounts, terms, and status (active, resolved, pending). Secured vs unsecured matters for buyer—secured debt stays with business, unsecured clears at close.

categories.title: Lease & Occupancy
categories.sub: If the Business Leases Its Space

questions.label: Base Term Remaining (months)
questions.prompt: How many months are left on the base lease term?
questions.hint: Buyers need runway—less than 12 months remaining is a deal killer. 3+ years = strong position. Options are critical; add them to the total.

questions.label: Option Period (months)
questions.prompt: How many months of option periods do they have?
questions.hint: Options are buyer gold—convert them to total remaining time. Ask about option terms: are they automatic, do they require notification, are there rent step-ups?

questions.label: Current Monthly Rent
questions.prompt: What's their current monthly rent?
questions.hint: Include NNN (triple net) and CAM charges if applicable. Get base + total occupancy cost. High rent relative to revenue = buyer red flag.

questions.label: Current on Rent?
questions.prompt: Are they current on rent, behind, or negotiating?
questions.hint: Behind = landlord relationship damaged and lease risk. Negotiating = deal leverage—ask what terms they're pushing for. Behind + sale = red flag.

questions.label: Lease Assignable / Transferable?
questions.prompt: Is the lease assignable or transferable to a buyer?
questions.hint: Non-assignable leases kill deals. LL Consent requires negotiation—timeline risk. Get a copy of the lease language on assignment terms before proceeding.

questions.label: Landlord Aware of Sale?
questions.prompt: Is the landlord aware they're planning to sell?
questions.hint: Landlord unaware = confidentiality risk and lease surprise. Get landlord consent early. Confidentiality is key until buyer + landlord alignment happens.

questions.label: Lease Notes
questions.prompt: Anything else important about the lease?
questions.hint: Capture exclusivity clauses, renewal terms, rent escalations, landlord financials (is LL stable?), and any landlord restrictions on concept changes.

questions.label: Has a Valuation Expectation?
questions.prompt: Do they have a price or valuation in mind?
questions.hint: "Open to Guidance" = easier negotiation. Formal appraisal = anchored expectations. Specific number = entrenched—assess if realistic before booking.

questions.label: Valuation Expectation
questions.prompt: What number or range are they expecting?
questions.hint: Get both the low and high. Ask how they arrived at these numbers. If no doc support, flag as "aspirational" and note what earnings justify.

questions.label: Expectations Realistic? (Rep’s Assessment)
questions.prompt: Your read — are their expectations realistic?
questions.hint: This is your gut check. Inflated = counseling conversation coming. Realistic = move forward. Addressable = show comps and financials to recalibrate.

questions.label: Prior Broker or Sale Attempt?
questions.prompt: Have they listed with a broker or tried to sell before?
questions.hint: Prior failed attempts = damaged price expectations. Get details: who, how long, why didn't work. First-time sellers need education on process and timeline.

questions.label: What Happened?
questions.prompt: What happened with that prior attempt?
questions.hint: Listen for blame-shifting vs. realistic lessons learned. If they blame the broker, dig into what actually happened. Bad process the first time = we fix it.

questions.label: Confidentiality Importance
questions.prompt: How important is confidentiality — high, medium, or low?
questions.hint: High = protect aggressively, NDA first, limited showings. Medium/Low = normal process. Ask WHY it matters; staff/competitor concerns are common red flags.

questions.label: Speaking With Other Brokers?
questions.prompt: Are they talking to other brokers right now?
questions.hint: Shopping around = commission pressure coming. First conversation = you have leverage and time to build trust. Unknown answer = they're likely talking to someone.

questions.label: RRG Rep Email — screening copy sent here
questions.prompt: What email should the screening copy go to?
questions.hint: This is your email. Screening summary will be sent here after call completes so you have documentation of what was discussed.

questions.label: Objections Raised on the Call
options: Needs to Talk to Partner / Accountant
questions.prompt: What objections or hesitations did they raise?
questions.hint: Flag every objection—these tell us why they might not move forward. Partner/Accountant input needed is normal. Price gap is addressable. Already has buyer = low probability.

questions.label: Call Notes
questions.placeholder: 3–4 sentences: motivation, financial picture, expectations, and your read on the lead. This goes into the contact's record in FullServe.
questions.prompt: Give me your 3–4 sentence summary — or hit Draft to generate one.
questions.hint: Capture the story: WHY they're selling, WHAT the financials show, WHAT they expect, and YOUR gut on deal viability. This is what someone reads six months from now.

questions.label: Recommended Path
questions.placeholder: Hit “✨ Draft from answers” — business sale, asset sale, or pass
questions.hint: The AI's read, not your decision. You still pick the Lead Status on the next card.

questions.label: Lead Status
questions.prompt: Your call — do we advance, nurture, pass, or refer this out?
questions.hint: Advance = move to next step. Nurture = stay in touch, revisit timeline. Pass = wrong deal. Refer Out = wrong geography/concept but solid operator elsewhere.
